model.name: Quality / Confidence
model.purpose: Attach quality dimensions, metric methods, scores and confidence or uncertainty statements to any host so an agent can create, inspect, compare, certify and operate quality claims without owning the host's identity, lineage, access or unit systems.
model.scope_statement: This mixin records fitness-for-purpose quality as observed, declared or certified properties of a host resource, including the dimension taxonomy, the metric and method used, the resulting score or qualitative judgement, the associated uncertainty or confidence, evaluation scope, policies and thresholds, evidence, and the lifecycle of the quality statement itself. It is format-neutral: JSON, YAML, RDF, HTML, Git, MCP and document stores are projections. It does not define a single universal meaning of quality; it provides a governed structure in which many assessors can state quality against named dimensions and methods.
in_scope: Identity, versioning and host binding of a quality assertion, measurement, annotation, certificate or quality-metadata container.
Quality categories, dimensions and characteristics, including inherent versus system-dependent views and domain extensions.
Alignment to published dimension sets (ISO/IEC 25012, ISO 19157-1, DQV, ISO/IEC 5259-2) without collapsing them into one taxonomy.
Metrics, expected value types, units of measure references, evaluation procedures, parameters, sampling and the data-quality unit or evaluation scope.
Quantitative and qualitative scores, pass/fail outcomes, composite and derived scores, and trade-off documentation.
Measurement uncertainty, coverage intervals, coverage probability or level of confidence, and ISO 19157 metaquality (confidence, representativity, homogeneity).
Predictive or model-reported confidence treated as a distinct, non-identical construct from metrological uncertainty.
Quality policies, thresholds, conformance and non-conformance, certificates, user feedback and supporting evidence.
Provenance, ownership, authority, validity window, invalidation, refresh, independent review, access, retention and audit of quality records.
Interoperability crosswalks, mapping conflicts and explicit non-conformance to sibling models (host identity, host provenance, access/privacy, units, QMS).
out_of_scope: Quality management systems, organisational process maturity and certification of organisations (ISO 9001 family) except as an optional referenced certificate about a host.
Software product quality characteristics in ISO/IEC 25010 (functionality, usability of software, maintainability) except where a host is data and ISO/IEC 25012 applies.
Authoritative identity of the host resource; this mixin only references the host.
Full provenance of the host's creation and lineage; only provenance of the quality assessment is in scope, via alignment to PROV.

Access control, confidentiality, privacy rights and security controls as first-class models, even though ISO/IEC 25012 lists confidentiality, accessibility and availability as data-quality characteristics.
Units of measure ontologies, coordinate reference systems and calendar systems, except as referenced attributes of a measurement.
Physical laboratory calibration processes and legal metrology beyond the GUM expression of uncertainty attached to a result.

Statistical survey production methodology as a whole (for example UNECE NQAF or GSBPM), clinical quality measures (FHIR/CMS) and SDMX quality reporting frameworks, which remain sibling or specialised alignments.

Fairness, safety, security and privacy of AI systems as trustworthiness characteristics; this mixin may record scores for those dimensions only when a named metric is supplied, and does not own those models.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Host identity and master-data identification models
boundary_notes.distinction: Quality statements reference a host; they do not mint or govern the host's authoritative identifier. A date, score or observation time is not a host identifier.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Provenance / lineage of the host (PROV-aligned sibling)
boundary_notes.distinction: PROV is used here for who generated, attributed, derived or invalidated the quality metadata or measurement, not as the canonical model of how the host itself was produced. DQV re-uses PROV for quality-metadata provenance and derivation among quality statements.

ISO/IEC 25012 includes confidentiality, accessibility and availability as data-quality characteristics. Those names may appear as aligned dimensions, but authorisation, disclosure control, encryption and privacy rights belong in sibling access/privacy models.
A quality value may carry a unit (DQV recommends sdmx-attribute:unitMeasure) and a GUM uncertainty, but the unit system, quantity kind and instrument model are not this mixin.

boundary_notes.neighbor: ISO 9001 quality management and organisational certification
boundary_notes.distinction: A dqv:QualityCertificate may point at a certificate document, including a management-system certificate, but this mixin does not model QMS clauses, audits of organisations, or people-engagement guidance.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Software product quality (ISO/IEC 25010) and AI trustworthiness characteristics as whole systems
boundary_notes.distinction: ISO/IEC 25012 is the data-quality model; NIST AI RMF trustworthiness (valid and reliable, safe, fair, and others) and ISO/IEC 5259 apply when the host is training or analytics data or when a quality score is about model outputs. Those system-level characteristics are alignments, not owned classifiers.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Requirements and policy models (ODRL or equivalent)
boundary_notes.distinction: DQV's QualityPolicy is an anchor to a policy vocabulary; thresholds, duties and permissions are referenced, not replaced.

sources.title: Data on the Web Best Practices: Data Quality Vocabulary (DQV)
sources.relevance: Normative vocabulary for quality categories, dimensions, metrics, measurements, policies, certificates, annotations, derivation and provenance of quality metadata; explicitly refuses a single definition of quality and attaches quality to datasets or other resources.

sources.title: ISO/IEC 25012:2008 Software engineering — Software product Quality Requirements and Evaluation (SQuaRE) — Data quality model
sources.organization: International Organization for Standardization / International Electrotechnical Commission
sources.relevance: Defines fifteen data-quality characteristics from inherent and system-dependent viewpoints; DQV and ISO/IEC 5259-2 treat this as the general data-quality characteristic catalogue.

sources.title: ISO 19157-1:2023 Geographic information — Data quality — Part 1: General requirements
sources.relevance: Authoritative structure for data-quality units, elements (completeness, logical consistency, positional accuracy, temporal quality, thematic quality), measures, evaluation procedures, reporting and metaquality; does not set minimum acceptable quality.

sources.title: ISO 8000-1:2022 Data quality — Part 1: Overview
sources.relevance: Establishes principles of information and data quality, the path to data quality, and the series architecture; treats relevant characteristics as purpose-dependent rather than absolute.

sources.title: JCGM 100:2008 Evaluation of measurement data — Guide to the expression of uncertainty in measurement (GUM 1995 with minor corrections)
sources.organization: Joint Committee for Guides in Metrology (BIPM, IEC, ILAC, ISO, IUPAC, IUPAP, IFCC, OIML)
sources.relevance: Normative rules for standard uncertainty, Type A and Type B evaluation, combined and expanded uncertainty, coverage factor and coverage probability or level of confidence attached to a measured result.

sources.title: NIST AI Risk Management Framework 1.0 — AI Risks and Trustworthiness and AI RMF Core (Measure)
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology (United States)
sources.version_or_date: AI RMF 1.0, 2023 (AIRC excerpts accessed 2026-08-23; revision in progress)
sources.relevance: Requires accuracy measurements with documented test sets and methods; Measure function demands associated measures of uncertainty, independent review, recalibration and documented TEVV; distinguishes validity, reliability, robustness and contextual trade-offs.

sources.title: ISO/IEC 5259-2:2024 Artificial intelligence — Data quality for analytics and machine learning (ML) — Part 2: Data quality measures
sources.relevance: Specifies a data-quality model, measures and reporting guidance for analytics and ML, building on ISO 8000, ISO/IEC 25012 and ISO/IEC 25024, and adding ML-oriented characteristics and measure identifiers such as Acc-ML-1/2.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.relevance: Canonical entity-activity-agent model used by DQV for generation, attribution, derivation, invalidation and bundles of quality metadata.

bundles.name: Identity and host binding
bundles.description: How a quality assertion, measurement, annotation, certificate or metadata container is identified and attached to one or more hosts, and how versions of those statements are distinguished.
bundles.rationale: DQV attaches quality information to a resource via computed-on, has-quality-measurement, annotation target and policy target; ISO 19157 evaluates a data-quality unit. Without stable identity and host binding, scores cannot be audited or compared.

layers.name: Quality assertion identity
layers.description: Identifiers, types and version tokens for quality statements as first-class records distinct from the host.

findings.name: Quality assertion identity
findings.description: Each quality measurement, annotation, certificate, policy binding or metadata container is a record with its own identifier. DQV treats a QualityMeasurement as an observation and QualityMetadata as a named container; PROV treats those records as entities that can be generated, attributed and invalidated. A calendar date is not an identifier.

questions.text: What is the authoritative master-system identifier of this quality assertion, and which identifier scheme (governed IRI, UUID or ULID) is used if no master identifier exists?
Is this record a measurement, annotation, certificate, policy binding, metadata container, or a derived composite statement?
Which version or revision of the quality statement is this, and which prior statement is it a revision of?
In which language or languages are labels and narrative quality comments provided?

data_elements.name: Assertion identifier
data_elements.description: Authoritative identifier of the quality statement.

data_elements.name: Assertion class
data_elements.description: Code for measurement, annotation, certificate, policy, container or composite.

data_elements.name: Statement version token
data_elements.description: Version of this quality statement, not of the host.

data_elements.name: Generation time
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 instant when the quality record was produced.

data_elements.name: Observation or evaluation event time
data_elements.description: When the quality property was observed or computed, distinct from ingestion time.

artifacts.name: Quality assertion record
artifacts.description: Canonical serialisable record for one quality statement including identifiers and class.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Master-system assertion identifier; else governed IRI in the Dimension namespace; else Dimension-assigned UUID or ULID.

findings.name: Host binding and evaluation target
findings.description: A quality statement is computed on or targeted at a host resource (dataset, distribution, feature collection, model output, metadata record, or finer subset). Inverse links allow a host to list its quality measurements. Multiple hosts or subsets may share a quality-metadata container.

questions.text: Which host resource or resources is this quality statement about, using the host's authoritative identifier?
Is the statement about the host data, about the host's metadata, or about a previous quality statement (quality of quality)?
If the host is only a subset, partition, distribution or linkset, what subset definition binds the evaluation?
Does the evaluation target a geographic extent or spatial object set, and in which spatial reference is that extent stated?

data_elements.name: Host identifier
data_elements.description: Reference to the resource whose quality is stated.

data_elements.name: Target kind
data_elements.description: Whether the host is data, metadata, a quality statement, a distribution or another resource class.

data_elements.name: Subset selector
data_elements.description: Query, filter, feature types or attribute paths that delimit the evaluated unit.

artifacts.name: Host binding stub
artifacts.description: Resolvable binding from quality assertion to host identifiers and optional subset selector.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Composite of assertion_id plus ordered host_ids; not a date.

bundles.name: Quality dimension system
bundles.description: Categories, dimensions and characteristics used to classify what aspect of quality is being spoken about, including standard catalogues and documented conflicts among them.
bundles.rationale: DQV models Category, Dimension and Metric as SKOS concepts and does not fix a single catalogue; ISO/IEC 25012, ISO 19157-1 and ISO/IEC 5259-2 each publish overlapping but non-identical characteristic sets. An agent must know which catalogue a score belongs to.

layers.name: Categories and dimensions
layers.description: Abstract quality characteristics grouped into categories; each dimension is expected to have one or more metrics.

findings.name: Quality category and dimension
findings.description: A dimension is a quality-related characteristic relevant to a consumer. A category groups dimensions that share a type of indicator. DQV represents both as SKOS concepts and warns that a dimension may sit in more than one category across frameworks, which new metrics should avoid.

questions.text: What is the identifier, preferred label and definition of the quality dimension being measured or annotated?
Which category or categories group this dimension, and is multiple categorisation intentional?
Which concept scheme or standard catalogue owns this dimension code?
Is this dimension treated as inherent to the data, system-dependent, or both, in the chosen catalogue?

data_elements.name: Dimension identifier
data_elements.description: Governed IRI or code for the dimension.

data_elements.name: Dimension definition
data_elements.description: Human-readable definition in a specified language.

data_elements.name: Category identifier
data_elements.description: Category grouping the dimension.

data_elements.name: Inherent or system-dependent viewpoint
data_elements.description: ISO/IEC 25012 viewpoint code: inherent, system-dependent, or both.

artifacts.name: Dimension registry entry
artifacts.description: Catalogue record for a quality dimension and its category membership.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Governed concept IRI in a named scheme; Dimension-assigned UUID only if no standard code exists.

layers.name: Standard dimension catalogues
layers.description: Published characteristic lists that an adopting Dimension may align to, with conflicts recorded rather than silently merged.

findings.name: ISO/IEC 25012 characteristic set
findings.description: ISO/IEC 25012 defines fifteen data-quality characteristics. Inherent: accuracy, completeness, consistency, credibility, currentness. Inherent and system-dependent: accessibility, compliance, confidentiality, efficiency, precision, traceability, understandability. System-dependent: availability, portability, recoverability. Definitions are always in a specific context of use.

questions.text: Which ISO/IEC 25012 characteristic, if any, does this dimension align to, using the official characteristic name?
What context of use is assumed when applying the ISO/IEC 25012 definition?
If uniqueness or validity is required by the adopting community, is it modelled as an extension rather than claimed as an ISO/IEC 25012 characteristic?
If confidentiality, accessibility or availability is selected, has the sibling access or privacy model been referenced instead of treating those scores as sufficient access control?

data_elements.name: ISO/IEC 25012 characteristic code
data_elements.description: One of the fifteen official characteristic names or a documented extension marker.

data_elements.name: Context of use
data_elements.description: Intended use context required by ISO/IEC 25012 definitions.

artifacts.name: ISO/IEC 25012 alignment note
artifacts.description: Record mapping a local dimension to an ISO/IEC 25012 characteristic and viewpoint.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Pair of local dimension_id and iso25012_characteristic_code.

findings.name: ISO 19157-1 quality element set
findings.description: ISO 19157-1:2023 defines components for describing geographic data quality: completeness (commission, omission), logical consistency (conceptual, domain, format, topological), positional accuracy (absolute, relative, gridded), temporal quality and thematic quality, plus metaquality elements and a process to add domain-specific components. Usability as a core element in ISO 19157:2013 is not retained as a 2023 core element. The standard does not set minimum acceptable quality.

questions.text: Which ISO 19157-1 data-quality element and sub-element, if any, does this dimension map to?
If a usability or fitness rating is recorded, is it modelled as an extension or policy outcome rather than as a 2023 core element?
What measure reference, evaluation method type and reporting descriptor are used for this geographic quality element?
Was a domain-specific quality component added under the ISO 19157-1 extension process, and who authorised it?

data_elements.name: ISO 19157-1 quality element
data_elements.description: Core element name such as completeness or logical consistency.

data_elements.name: ISO 19157-1 sub-element
data_elements.description: Sub-element such as omission, domain consistency or absolute positional accuracy.

data_elements.name: Measure reference
data_elements.description: Identifier of the data-quality measure used in reporting.

artifacts.name: Geographic data-quality report section
artifacts.description: ISO 19157-aligned reporting block for one quality unit and element.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Quality unit identifier plus element and measure reference; not a report date.

findings.name: Competing taxonomies and mapping conflicts
findings.description: DQV states that quality lies in the eye of the beholder and ships both ISO/IEC 25012 and Linked Data dimension examples. ISO 8000 treats relevant characteristics as purpose-dependent. DAMA-style uniqueness is not an ISO/IEC 25012 characteristic. Precision in ISO/IEC 25012 and DQV (resolution) is not GUM expanded uncertainty. These conflicts must be recorded, not smoothed.

questions.text: Which known mapping conflicts apply to this dimension (uniqueness, usability, precision versus uncertainty, credibility versus confidence, fitness versus intrinsic accuracy)?
Is this dimension's applicability declared as intrinsic, or only as fitness for a stated purpose under ISO 8000 principles?
Which local profile or concept scheme is canonical for this Dimension when catalogues disagree?

data_elements.name: Mapping conflict code
data_elements.description: Coded conflict between catalogues.

data_elements.name: Canonical concept scheme
data_elements.description: IRI of the scheme that wins locally.

artifacts.name: Dimension crosswalk
artifacts.description: Table mapping local dimensions to ISO/IEC 25012, ISO 19157-1, DQV examples and ISO/IEC 5259-2, with conflict flags.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Crosswalk version IRI plus row key of local dimension_id.

layers.name: Domain-specific dimension extension
layers.description: ISO 19157-1 and ISO/IEC 5259-2 allow additional characteristics; DQV allows new SKOS dimensions. Extensions must be identified, defined and not presented as ISO core codes.

findings.name: Domain-specific dimension extension
findings.description: Additional dimensions (for example ML-specific characteristics in ISO/IEC 5259-2, linked-data interlinking, or community uniqueness) are first-class local concepts with provenance of who added them. The full list of extra ISO/IEC 5259-2 characteristics is not fully extractable from freely published text and remains a documented gap.

questions.text: What identifier and definition distinguish this extension dimension from standard catalogue codes?
Who authorised the extension and against which standard extension clause?
If an ISO/IEC 5259-2 additional ML characteristic is claimed, is the official characteristic name cited from the standard text rather than inferred?

data_elements.name: Extension dimension identifier
data_elements.description: Local IRI for a non-core dimension.

data_elements.name: Evidence gap flag
data_elements.description: True if the official characteristic list was not available from a primary extract.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Extension dimensions are concept records stored in the dimension registry; no separate binary artefact is required beyond the registry entry already defined for dimensions.

bundles.name: Metric and method
bundles.description: The procedure that turns an abstract dimension into an observable indicator, including expected datatype, unit, parameters and evaluation method.
bundles.rationale: DQV requires a Metric with expected datatype and dimension; ISO 19157 specifies measure content structure and evaluation procedures; ISO/IEC 5259-2 and ISO/IEC 25024 supply named measurement functions. A score without a method is not comparable.

layers.name: Metric definition
layers.description: Named, reusable measurement standard for a dimension.

findings.name: Quality metric
findings.description: A metric is a standard to measure a dimension. An observation assigns a value in a given unit to that metric. Multiple metrics may exist per dimension. Values may be numeric or boolean. DQV does not recommend subclassing Metric in OWL to capture constraints; parameters are extra properties on the measurement.

questions.text: What is the identifier, definition and owning dimension of this metric?
What expected datatype and allowed value range or enumeration does the metric declare?
What unit of measure, if any, applies, and which unit system IRI is referenced?
Is this metric derived from another metric, and if so from which?

data_elements.name: Metric identifier
data_elements.description: Governed identifier of the metric.

data_elements.name: Expected datatype
data_elements.description: Datatype of observed values such as boolean or double.

data_elements.name: Unit of measure IRI
data_elements.description: Reference to a unit in an external unit system.

data_elements.name: In dimension
data_elements.description: Dimension this metric measures.

artifacts.name: Metric specification
artifacts.description: Reusable specification of a metric, datatype, unit and dimension.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Governed metric IRI in a metric catalogue; UUID only if locally minted.

layers.name: Evaluation procedure and parameters
layers.description: How the metric is computed, including method type, parameters, tools, human versus automated evaluation and ISO 19157 evaluation descriptors.

findings.name: Evaluation method and parameters
findings.description: ISO 19157 describes evaluation procedures and descriptors of measures. DQV measurements may carry extra parameters (language, property, and others). NIST requires that accuracy measurements be paired with clearly defined test sets representative of expected use and with details of test methodology. Independent review is recommended.

questions.text: Is the evaluation direct or indirect, internal or external, automated, manual or mixed, and which procedure identifier is used?
Which metric parameters (thresholds inside the method, language, property path, test-set identifier) were bound for this run?
Was the method or result independently reviewed, and by whom?
Which software agent or human agent executed the evaluation?

data_elements.name: Evaluation method type
data_elements.description: Coded method class for how quality was evaluated.

data_elements.name: Procedure identifier
data_elements.description: Reference to the written or executable procedure.

data_elements.name: Parameter map
data_elements.description: Bound parameters for this evaluation run.

data_elements.name: Test set identifier
data_elements.description: Representative test or reference set used, required for accuracy-style measures.

artifacts.name: Evaluation procedure specification
artifacts.description: Versioned procedure describing steps, parameters, tools and acceptance of independent review.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Procedure identifier plus version; not the run date.

bundles.name: Score and result
bundles.description: The observed quality value, its scale, aggregation and derivation from other measurements.
bundles.rationale: DQV's dqv:value is the metric result; composite scores and trade-offs appear in NIST measurement practice and in derived DQV measurements via prov:wasDerivedFrom.

layers.name: Measurement value
layers.description: Atomic observed score or qualitative result for one metric on one host binding.

findings.name: Quality measurement value
findings.description: A QualityMeasurement is an evaluation of a host against a metric, carrying a value and optional unit. Values may be quantitative, boolean or qualitative. Precision (resolution) and accuracy are distinct metrics in DQV examples and must not be stored as one undifferentiated score.

questions.text: What is the observed value, its datatype, unit and scale type (ratio, interval, ordinal, nominal, boolean)?
Does a larger numeric value mean better quality for this metric, and what is the theoretically best or worst value?
If the result is qualitative, which controlled code or ordinal label was assigned and by which scheme?
If no value could be computed (empty host, missing reference, failed run), what exception code explains the missing score?

data_elements.name: Observed value
data_elements.description: Literal result of the metric.

data_elements.name: Scale type
data_elements.description: Measurement scale of the value.

data_elements.name: Polarity
data_elements.description: Whether higher is better, lower is better, or target is best.

data_elements.name: Missing-value exception
data_elements.description: Why a value is absent.

artifacts.name: Measurement observation
artifacts.description: Immutable observation of one metric value on one host binding.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Assertion identifier of the measurement; observations are not overwritten in place.

layers.name: Aggregation and derivation
layers.description: Composite scores, roll-ups across partitions, and measurements derived from other measurements.

findings.name: Composite and derived score
findings.description: DQV allows measurements, metrics and annotations to be derived from others via prov:wasDerivedFrom. NIST notes trade-offs among characteristics and requires a traceable basis for management decisions including recalibration. Hidden weights make a composite score non-auditable.

questions.text: Which source measurements, metrics or annotations were used to derive this result?
What weights, operators or rules combined the inputs, and are those weights disclosed?
Which trustworthiness or quality trade-offs were accepted when producing the composite, and who decided?
Is this score a roll-up across partitions, and is homogeneity or disaggregation available for those partitions?

data_elements.name: Source assertions
data_elements.description: Measurements or annotations this result was derived from.

data_elements.name: Weight map
data_elements.description: Disclosed weights per input dimension or metric.

data_elements.name: Combination operator
data_elements.description: Rule such as weighted mean, minimum, or conjunction of pass/fail.

artifacts.name: Score derivation record
artifacts.description: Trace from composite score back to inputs, weights and decision.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Derived assertion identifier plus derivation activity identifier.

bundles.name: Confidence, uncertainty and metaquality
bundles.description: How sure the assessor is, how dispersed the possible values of a measurand are, and the quality of the quality evaluation itself. These constructs are related but not interchangeable.
bundles.rationale: GUM expresses uncertainty of measurement with coverage intervals. ISO 19157 metaquality describes confidence in quality results, representativity and homogeneity. NIST requires measures of uncertainty alongside performance metrics. ML or rater 'confidence' scores are a separate construct unless calibrated and declared.

layers.name: Metrological uncertainty
layers.description: GUM evaluation of dispersion of values that could reasonably be attributed to a measurand.

findings.name: Measurement uncertainty
findings.description: Standard uncertainty is the uncertainty of a result expressed as a standard deviation. Type A evaluation uses statistical analysis of observations; Type B uses other means. Combined standard uncertainty is propagated through the measurement model. Expanded uncertainty U equals coverage factor k times combined standard uncertainty.

questions.text: What is the standard or combined standard uncertainty of this result, in which unit, and was evaluation Type A, Type B or both?
Which input quantities and uncertainty components form the uncertainty budget?
Does the GUM linearised model apply, or is a different uncertainty evaluation (for example Monte Carlo as in later JCGM documents) used?
If the quality result is ordinal or nominal, how is uncertainty expressed without falsely quoting a GUM expanded uncertainty?

data_elements.name: Standard uncertainty
data_elements.description: Uncertainty expressed as a standard deviation.

data_elements.name: Combined standard uncertainty
data_elements.description: Uncertainty of the output quantity after combining inputs.

data_elements.name: Type A or Type B evaluation
data_elements.description: GUM evaluation type.

data_elements.name: Uncertainty budget components
data_elements.description: List of contributing uncertainties.

artifacts.name: Uncertainty budget
artifacts.description: Documented components, model and combined uncertainty for a quantitative quality result.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Budget identifier tied to the measurement assertion identifier.

layers.name: Coverage interval and confidence level
layers.description: Interval about a result expected to encompass a large fraction of the distribution of values attributable to the measurand.

findings.name: Coverage interval and confidence level
findings.description: Expanded uncertainty defines an interval Y ± U. The coverage factor k is chosen for a desired coverage probability; k approximately 2 is commonly associated with about 95 percent coverage for near-normal cases. GUM cautions that statistical terms confidence interval and confidence level apply only under stated conditions; coverage probability is the preferred general term. Later GUM-1:2023 language emphasises a coverage interval for a specified coverage probability.

questions.text: What expanded uncertainty, coverage factor, coverage probability and interval bounds accompany this result?
What probability distribution or approximation justifies the coverage factor?
Is the reported figure labelled as coverage probability, GUM level of confidence, or a statistical confidence interval, and is that label justified?
If an interval is reported without k or coverage probability, what exception or incompleteness is recorded?

data_elements.name: Expanded uncertainty
data_elements.description: U = k times combined standard uncertainty.

data_elements.name: Coverage factor
data_elements.description: Factor k used to obtain expanded uncertainty.

data_elements.name: Coverage probability
data_elements.description: Probability associated with the coverage interval.

data_elements.name: Interval lower bound
data_elements.description: Lower bound of the coverage interval.

data_elements.name: Confidence term used
data_elements.description: Whether coverage probability, level of confidence or confidence interval was claimed.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Coverage interval figures are numeric attributes of a measurement observation and the uncertainty budget; they are not a separate serial artefact unless a laboratory issues a calibration certificate, which is modelled under certificates.

layers.name: Metaquality of the evaluation
layers.description: ISO 19157 metaquality describes the quality of the quality description, including confidence in the result, representativity of the evaluation, and homogeneity of quality across the data.

findings.name: Metaquality
findings.description: A quality report can itself be wrong, biased or unrepresentative. Metaquality elements record confidence in the quality evaluation, whether the evaluated sample represents the quality unit, and whether quality is homogeneous across the unit. This is quality-of-quality, not a second copy of the host score.

questions.text: What metaquality confidence is assigned to this quality result, and on what evidence?
How representative of the declared quality unit is the evaluated sample or census?
Is quality homogeneous across the unit, or do partitions differ enough that a single score is misleading?
Who assessed metaquality, and is that party independent of the original assessor?

data_elements.name: Metaquality confidence
data_elements.description: Stated confidence in the quality evaluation.

data_elements.name: Representativity statement
data_elements.description: How the evaluation represents the quality unit.

data_elements.name: Homogeneity flag
data_elements.description: Whether quality is treated as homogeneous across the unit.

artifacts.name: Metaquality statement
artifacts.description: Record of confidence, representativity and homogeneity about a quality result.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Metaquality assertion identifier referencing the evaluated quality assertion.

layers.name: Predictive and rater confidence
layers.description: Model-reported scores, rater certainty and NIST-style measures of uncertainty for AI outputs, kept distinct from GUM coverage.

findings.name: Predictive and AI confidence
findings.description: NIST requires performance assessment with associated measures of uncertainty, representative test sets and possible recalibration. ISO/IEC 5259-2 provides ML-oriented accuracy measures such as syntactic and semantic data accuracy. A softmax, logit or stars-out-of-five rater score is not a GUM expanded uncertainty unless a calibration study justifies a coverage interpretation.

questions.text: What predictive or rater confidence score was produced, on what scale, and is it claimed to be a calibrated probability?
Is a mapping to GUM coverage explicitly not claimed for this predictive score?
When was this confidence measure last calibrated or recalibrated against a representative test set, and what drift triggered it?
Are accuracy or confidence figures disaggregated for data segments relevant to expected use?

data_elements.name: Predictive confidence score
data_elements.description: Model or rater reported score.

data_elements.name: Calibrated probability flag
data_elements.description: Whether the score is a calibrated probability.

data_elements.name: Declared construct
data_elements.description: Code distinguishing predictive score, rater certainty, GUM coverage and metaquality confidence.

artifacts.name: Confidence calibration report
artifacts.description: Evidence that a predictive score was or was not calibrated to observed frequencies on a stated test set.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Calibration study identifier; not the model training date.

bundles.name: Evaluation scope and fitness for purpose
bundles.description: The data-quality unit, sampling design, spatial and temporal window, and the purpose against which fitness is judged.
bundles.rationale: ISO 19157 evaluates a quality unit and does not set minimum acceptable quality; ISO/IEC 25012 and ISO 8000 make quality depend on context of use; DQV likewise treats fitness as consumer judgement.

layers.name: Quality unit and evaluation window
layers.description: Scope of features, attributes, time and space covered by the evaluation.

findings.name: Evaluation scope and quality unit
findings.description: ISO 19157-1 defines the data-quality unit as the scoped combination of data on which quality elements are evaluated. Scope may be a dataset series, dataset, subset, attribute, or spatial/temporal window. Currentness (ISO/IEC 25012) and temporal quality (ISO 19157) require explicit time bounds.

questions.text: What is the identifier and definition of the data-quality unit evaluated?
What temporal extent of the host was evaluated, and is that distinct from the time the evaluation ran?
What spatial extent, if any, bounds the quality unit?
For streaming or continuously updated hosts, what sliding window or watermark defines currentness evaluation?

data_elements.name: Quality unit identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of the scoped unit of evaluation.

data_elements.name: Host temporal extent start
data_elements.description: Start of the host time range evaluated.

data_elements.name: Host temporal extent end
data_elements.description: End of the host time range evaluated.

data_elements.name: Currentness window
data_elements.description: Duration used for streaming currentness.

artifacts.name: Quality unit definition
artifacts.description: Scoped definition of what was evaluated, including spatial and temporal windows.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Quality unit identifier assigned by the evaluation authority.

layers.name: Sampling and representativity
layers.description: Whether the evaluation was a census or a sample, and how the sample relates to the unit.

findings.name: Sampling and representativity
findings.description: Quality may be evaluated on all objects or on a sample. ISO 19157 metaquality includes representativity. NIST requires test sets representative of expected use. An empty sample is an exception, not a perfect score.

questions.text: Was the evaluation a full census of the quality unit or a sample, and what was the sample size and design?
What sampling frame, inclusion rules and exclusion rules were used?
If the sample or unit was empty, what exception was raised instead of reporting 100 percent completeness?
Is the sample or test set representative of the conditions of expected use, including relevant segments?

data_elements.name: Census flag
data_elements.description: True if the whole quality unit was evaluated.

data_elements.name: Sample size
data_elements.description: Number of evaluated items.

data_elements.name: Sampling design
data_elements.description: Design code such as simple random, stratified, or judgement.

artifacts.name: Sampling design record
artifacts.description: Design, frame, size and representativity claims for an evaluation.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Sampling design identifier referenced by the quality unit.

layers.name: Fitness for purpose and context of use
layers.description: Quality as fitness rather than an absolute property of data.

findings.name: Context of use and fitness
findings.description: DQV does not define quality objectively; ISO/IEC 25012 definitions are in a specific context of use; ISO 8000-1 establishes principles of information and data quality and a path to data quality for specified kinds of data. A host may be fit for one purpose and unfit for another. Minimum acceptable levels belong in a product specification or quality policy, not in ISO 19157 itself.

questions.text: For which stated purpose, user class and process is this quality claim made?
Who judged fitness for that purpose, and is the judgement a consumer annotation, a producer declaration, or a policy conformance result?
Are there declared purposes for which this host is explicitly not claimed to be fit?
Which data product specification or quality policy, if any, states minimum acceptable quality for this purpose?

data_elements.name: Purpose identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of the intended use.

data_elements.name: Fitness judgement
data_elements.description: Coded fitness outcome for the stated purpose.

data_elements.name: Limitations of use
data_elements.description: Stated purposes or conditions for which fitness is not claimed.

artifacts.name: Fitness-for-purpose statement
artifacts.description: Declared purpose, judge, outcome and limitations.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Fitness statement identifier composed with purpose_id and host_id.

bundles.name: Policy, conformance and evidence
bundles.description: Requirements, thresholds, pass/fail, certificates, annotations, user feedback and supporting evidence for quality claims.
bundles.rationale: DQV models QualityPolicy, dcterms:conformsTo, QualityCertificate, QualityAnnotation and UserQualityFeedback, and allows grouping under QualityMetadata. Evidence is required to avoid unsubstantiated conformance claims.

layers.name: Quality policy and thresholds
layers.description: Agreements and numeric or logical constraints that quality measurements are expected to satisfy.

findings.name: Quality policy and threshold
findings.description: A QualityPolicy is a policy or agreement chiefly governed by data quality concerns. DQV shows ODRL duties constrained by a metric, for example endpoint availability greater than or equal to 99 percent. Thresholds must cite the metric, operator and comparison value.

questions.text: What policy identifier, issuer, assignee and target host define this quality policy?
What metric, operator and threshold value constitute the duty or constraint?
Which quality dimensions does the policy govern?
Is the policy an open offer, a bilateral agreement, or an internal rule, and who may waive it?

data_elements.name: Policy identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of the quality policy.

data_elements.name: Comparison operator
data_elements.description: Operator such as greater-than-or-equal.

data_elements.name: Threshold value
data_elements.description: Comparison value bound to the metric.

artifacts.name: Quality policy document
artifacts.description: Serial policy or agreement with metric constraints.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Policy identifier issued by the policy authority.

layers.name: Conformance and exceptions
layers.description: Whether a host or its metadata conforms to a standard or policy, including explicit non-conformance.

findings.name: Conformance and exception
findings.description: DQV uses dcterms:conformsTo for standards and QualityPolicy for quality agreements. Finer non-conformance reporting is acknowledged as future work in DQV. ISO 19157 reports quality against a product specification without itself defining pass thresholds. A pass/fail outcome must cite the measurement, the threshold and the decision time.

questions.text: To which standard, profile or policy is conformance claimed, and at which version?
What is the pass, fail or not-evaluated outcome, based on which measurements?
If non-conforming, which constraints failed and what exception or waiver applies?
Which required checks were not executed, and is untested distinct from pass?

data_elements.name: Standard or profile identifier
data_elements.description: Referenced standard for conformance.

data_elements.name: Conformance outcome
data_elements.description: Pass, fail, not-evaluated, waived or partial.

data_elements.name: Waiver identifier
data_elements.description: Authorised waiver of a failed constraint.

artifacts.name: Conformance statement
artifacts.description: Decision record linking measurements to a standard or policy outcome.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Conformance statement identifier; not the date of the standard.

layers.name: Certificates, annotations and feedback
layers.description: Third-party certificates and human quality annotations, including questions and ratings.

findings.name: Quality certificate
findings.description: A QualityCertificate is an annotation that associates a host with another resource that certifies quality according to assessment rules. The class name is slightly misleading: the DQV instance is the annotation pointing at the certificate document, not the certificate file itself.

questions.text: What identifier, issuer, scheme and validity period apply to the referenced certificate?
Where is the certificate document stored, and what integrity hash binds it?
Which hosts, dimensions and sites does the certificate actually cover?
Has the certificate been revoked or suspended, when, and by whom?

data_elements.name: Certificate identifier
data_elements.description: Issuer-assigned certificate identifier.

data_elements.name: Certificate issuer
data_elements.description: Agent that issued the certificate.

data_elements.name: Valid from
data_elements.description: Start of certificate validity.

data_elements.name: Valid to
data_elements.description: End of certificate validity.

data_elements.name: Revocation status
data_elements.description: Current revocation or suspension state.

artifacts.name: Quality certificate document
artifacts.description: The document or token that certifies quality, distinct from the DQV annotation that points to it.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Issuer certificate identifier plus issuer identifier; integrity hash required.

findings.name: Quality annotation and user feedback
findings.description: Quality annotations include ratings, certificates and feedback motivated by quality assessment. UserQualityFeedback additionally uses Web Annotation motivations to distinguish classifications, questions and other feedback. Multiple independent assessors may disagree.

questions.text: What annotation motivation and body (rating, text, classification, question) does this feedback carry?
Who authored the annotation, in which role (producer, consumer, aggregator, certifier), and is the author independent?
Does this annotation conflict with other assessments of the same host and dimension, and how is disagreement recorded?
Are the annotator's identity and comment subject to privacy or access restrictions?

data_elements.name: Annotation motivation
data_elements.description: Web Annotation motivation, including quality assessment.

data_elements.name: Rating value
data_elements.description: Optional ordinal or numeric rating.

data_elements.name: Author agent
data_elements.description: Agent who created the annotation.

artifacts.name: Quality annotation body
artifacts.description: Body of a quality annotation or user feedback item.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Annotation identifier from the annotation system; else UUID assigned by the Dimension.

layers.name: Supporting evidence
layers.description: Observations, logs, test outputs and reports that justify a score, certificate or annotation.

findings.name: Supporting evidence
findings.description: NIST requires formalised reporting of TEVV results. DQV groups statements in QualityMetadata so provenance can be tracked jointly. A score without evidence is a claim, not a completed evaluation.

questions.text: Which evidence items (logs, test outputs, samples, reviewer notes) support this quality statement?
What integrity hash, generation time and generating activity bind each evidence item?
Did the independent reviewer judge the evidence sufficient for the claimed outcome?

data_elements.name: Evidence item identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of a supporting artefact.

data_elements.name: Integrity hash
data_elements.description: Cryptographic hash of the evidence bytes.

artifacts.name: Quality evidence pack
artifacts.description: Bundle of supporting files and hashes for a quality statement.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Evidence pack identifier tied to the quality assertion; hashes of members recorded.

bundles.name: Governance, lifecycle and interoperability
bundles.description: Provenance, ownership, validity, invalidation, refresh, access, retention, audit and crosswalks for quality records.
bundles.rationale: DQV documents provenance of quality metadata and measurements with PROV. PROV invalidation models withdrawn statements. Quality claims expire as hosts change. Access and retention apply to quality records even when the host has a different policy.

layers.name: Provenance of quality metadata
layers.description: Who generated, attributed, used and derived quality records.

findings.name: Quality assessment provenance
findings.description: QualityMetadata may record wasGeneratedBy, wasAttributedTo and wasDerivedFrom. A measurement may have its own generation activity, software agent and human assessor. This is provenance of the assessment, not of the host. Bundles allow provenance of provenance.

questions.text: Which activity generated this quality record, started and ended at which RFC 3339 times?
Which agent is the quality record attributed to, and on whose behalf did they act?
Which procedures, test sets, reference data and prior measurements were used?
Which quality-metadata bundle or named graph contains this statement for joint provenance?

data_elements.name: Generating activity
data_elements.description: PROV activity that produced the quality record.

data_elements.name: Attributed agent
data_elements.description: Agent responsible for the quality record.

data_elements.name: Quality metadata container
data_elements.description: Container grouping related quality statements.

artifacts.name: Quality metadata bundle
artifacts.description: Named container of quality statements with joint provenance.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Bundle or QualityMetadata IRI; adding or removing a statement yields a new bundle identity as in PROV.

layers.name: Validity, invalidation and refresh
layers.description: When a quality statement is current, superseded or withdrawn, including host-change triggers.

findings.name: Quality statement lifecycle
findings.description: PROV entities can be generated and invalidated. Currentness of data is an ISO/IEC 25012 characteristic; currentness of a quality claim is a lifecycle property of the statement. Host revision, distribution shift, certificate revocation or failed monitoring should invalidate or refresh measurements rather than silently overwrite them. NIST Manage includes recalibration and removal from use.

questions.text: During which RFC 3339 interval is this quality statement intended to be used?
Has the statement been invalidated, by which activity, at what time, and for what reason?
What events (host version change, elapsed time, drift metric, incident) require re-evaluation?
Which newer statement supersedes this one for the same host, metric and scope?

data_elements.name: Statement valid from
data_elements.description: Start of intended use of the quality statement.

data_elements.name: Statement valid to
data_elements.description: End of intended use of the quality statement.

data_elements.name: Invalidated at
data_elements.description: Instant the quality entity was invalidated.

data_elements.name: Refresh triggers
data_elements.description: Event types that require a new evaluation.

artifacts.name: Quality lifecycle event log
artifacts.description: Append-only generation, invalidation, supersession and refresh events.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Event identifier (UUID or ULID) plus assertion identifier; event time is not the identifier.

layers.name: Access, retention and audit
layers.description: Who may read or change quality records, how long they are kept, and what is audited.

findings.name: Access, retention and audit
findings.description: Quality scores may be sensitive (they can reveal defects, security posture or personal data in comments). Default access is narrower than public host catalogues. Retention of quality evidence may exceed or be shorter than host retention. Audit must record create, invalidate and access of quality records. Confidentiality as an ISO/IEC 25012 characteristic of the host is not a substitute for access control on the quality store.

questions.text: Who may read this quality statement by default, and which scopes (bundle, layer, finding, artefact) are separately controlled?
Does this quality record reveal security, safety or personal data that requires tighter classification?
What retention period, legal hold and deletion method apply to the quality statement and its evidence pack?
Which audit events must be recorded for this quality record, and for how long?

data_elements.name: Default read roles
data_elements.description: Roles allowed to read the quality record.

data_elements.name: Sensitivity classification
data_elements.description: Classification of the quality record.

data_elements.name: Retention period
data_elements.description: Retention duration for the quality record.

data_elements.name: Legal hold flag
data_elements.description: Whether deletion is blocked.

artifacts.name: Quality record access and retention policy
artifacts.description: Policy governing access, retention, deletion and audit of quality records.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Policy identifier issued by the Dimension owner.

layers.name: Interoperability crosswalks
layers.description: Mappings to DQV, ISO catalogues, GUM constructs and AI quality measures without claiming false conformance.

findings.name: Interoperability crosswalk
findings.description: Adopting Dimensions should publish mappings from local fields to dqv:QualityMeasurement, ISO/IEC 25012 characteristics, ISO 19157-1 elements, GUM uncertainty fields and ISO/IEC 5259-2 measure identifiers. Absence of a mapping is a gap, not implicit conformance.

questions.text: Which local fields map to DQV classes and properties, and which DQV features are unimplemented?
Which local dimensions map to ISO/IEC 25012, ISO 19157-1 and ISO/IEC 5259-2 identifiers?
Is any formal conformance to those standards claimed, and if so where is the evidence?

data_elements.name: DQV class map
data_elements.description: Mapping of local types to DQV classes.

data_elements.name: Conformance claim flag
data_elements.description: Whether formal conformance is asserted.

artifacts.name: Quality mixin interoperability crosswalk
artifacts.description: Versioned mapping tables to DQV, ISO and GUM constructs.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Crosswalk version IRI.

functions.name: Attach quality assertion
functions.description: Bind a new quality measurement, annotation, certificate reference or policy binding to a host using the host's authoritative identifier and a new assertion identifier.
outputs: quality assertion record with assertion_id and host binding
preconditions: Host identifier is resolvable in the host identity model.
Caller is permitted to create quality records for that host.
effects: A new quality entity is generated and attributed.
The host inverse quality list is updated.

functions.name: Register dimension and metric
functions.description: Add or version a dimension and metric in the Dimension's catalogue, including expected datatype, unit reference and catalogue alignments.
preconditions: Registrar is the dimension steward or delegate.
Alignment conflicts are either resolved or recorded.
effects: New metrics become available for evaluation.

functions.name: Evaluate metric
functions.description: Run an evaluation procedure on a quality unit and record an immutable measurement observation.
outputs: optional exception for empty or failed evaluation
preconditions: Metric and procedure are registered.
Quality unit is defined.
Test set is representative when the metric is an accuracy-style measure.
effects: A QualityMeasurement is generated with event time and ingestion time.
Evidence pack hashes may be attached.

functions.name: Express uncertainty or confidence
functions.description: Attach a GUM uncertainty, coverage interval, metaquality statement or predictive confidence construct to a measurement, with an explicit construct code.
outputs: updated measurement with uncertainty or a linked metaquality statement
preconditions: Construct code distinguishes GUM coverage, metaquality confidence and predictive scores.
Expanded uncertainty is not stored without k or coverage probability unless incompleteness is flagged.
effects: Consumers can filter on declared construct.
Mislabeling of softmax scores as GUM confidence is prevented by constraint.

functions.name: Decide conformance
functions.description: Compare measurements to a quality policy or standard and record pass, fail, waived or not-evaluated.
preconditions: Thresholds cite metric, operator and value.
Untested required checks are not recorded as pass.
effects: Host conformance state is updated for that policy version.

functions.name: Issue or revoke quality certificate
functions.description: Create a QualityCertificate annotation pointing at a certificate document, or revoke it.
preconditions: Issuer is a recognised certifying body for the scheme.
Integrity hash of the document is recorded.
effects: Hosts gain or lose certified status.

functions.name: Ingest quality feedback
functions.description: Accept a user or aggregator annotation, including conflicting assessments.
preconditions: Motivation includes quality assessment.
Privacy classification of the comment is set.
effects: Disagreement with existing assessments is linked, not overwritten.

functions.name: Derive composite score
functions.description: Compute a derived measurement from other measurements with disclosed operators and weights.
preconditions: All sources exist and share a compatible quality unit or documented roll-up.
Weights are stored when a weighted operator is used.
effects: Trade-off notes may be attached for management review.

functions.name: Invalidate or refresh quality statement
functions.description: Invalidate a quality entity and optionally trigger a new evaluation after host change, elapsed time, drift or incident.
preconditions: Caller has update authority or an automated trigger policy matches.
Legal hold is not set if deletion is requested; invalidation is still allowed.
effects: Supersession link is set when a replacement exists.

functions.name: Crosswalk dimension
functions.description: Record or update a mapping from a local dimension or field to external catalogues without implying conformance.
preconditions: Target codes are cited from a named standard version.
effects: Unmapped locals remain visible as gaps.

composition.target: Any host entity, event or artefact in the adopting Dimension
composition.purpose: Attach quality dimensions, methods, scores and confidence to hosts without becoming the host identity model.
Reuse Category, Dimension, Metric, QualityMeasurement, QualityPolicy, QualityAnnotation, QualityCertificate, QualityMetadata and derivation patterns as the primary web-native alignment.
Optional characteristic catalogue and inherent versus system-dependent viewpoint.
Quality unit, element/sub-element catalogue, evaluation procedures, reporting descriptors and metaquality when hosts are geographic or similarly structured.
Principles of information and data quality and purpose-dependent characteristic selection.
Expression of measurement uncertainty, coverage factor and coverage probability for quantitative results.
Analytics and machine-learning quality measures and reporting when the host is training, evaluation or production inference data.
Generation, attribution, derivation, invalidation and bundles for quality metadata; not a substitute for host lineage.
Unit of measure IRIs and quantity kinds carried on scores; this mixin does not own the unit system.
Resolve authoritative host identifiers used in computed-on and annotation targets.

composition.target: Access, privacy and security sibling models
composition.purpose: Govern access to quality records and avoid treating ISO/IEC 25012 confidentiality or availability scores as access control.
Express QualityPolicy duties, permissions and waivers.

composition.target: NIST AI RMF Measure and trustworthiness characteristics
composition.purpose: Uncertainty alongside accuracy, representative test sets, independent review, recalibration and documented trade-offs for AI-related hosts.

owner_package_requirements: Designate a quality steward accountable for the local dimension and metric catalogue, alignment decisions and conflict register.
Publish a versioned namespace for assertion, dimension, metric, policy and certificate identifiers, with IRI stewardship.
Maintain an assessment authority matrix stating who may evaluate, certify, waive, independently review, invalidate and read each class of quality record.
Provide AGENTS.md plus Specification, Storage type, Interface and Processes URLs before agents write quality data, including when storage is MongoDB or MCP.
Keep a legal-hold and retention schedule for quality evidence distinct from host retention.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Use the adopting Dimension's governed namespace under nav path NAV.XCT.QLT (for example a Dimension IRI stem plus /qlt/assertion/, /qlt/dimension/, /qlt/metric/). Do not mint host identifiers in this namespace. Prefer standard concept IRIs (dqv, ISO codes) when aligning; otherwise assign UUID or ULID only after confirming no master-system identifier exists.
registry_links: ISO/IEC 5259-2 measure identifiers where licensed text is available

canonicalization_rules: Store each measurement as an immutable observation with assertion_id, host binding, metric_id, value, scale, optional unit IRI, evaluation event time and ingestion time as separate RFC 3339 timestamps.
Require an explicit construct code when any confidence or uncertainty field is present: gum-coverage, metaquality-confidence, predictive-score, rater-certainty, or other documented construct.
Canonical dimension and metric identifiers are IRIs or codes in a named scheme version; labels are language-tagged and not identifiers.
Composite scores MUST persist disclosed operators and weights.
Do not treat a calendar date as an identifier.
patch_rules: Corrections create a new measurement linked with derivation or revision; they do not silently overwrite values.
Invalidation is an explicit PROV-style event with reason; deletion of current pointers is not a substitute for invalidation history.
Catalogue patches (new dimensions, metric parameter changes) increment catalogue version and do not rewrite historical observations.
Certificate revocation patches the certificate entity's lifecycle, not the historical annotation that it was once issued.
compatibility_rules: Alignments to DQV, ISO/IEC 25012, ISO 19157-1, GUM and ISO/IEC 5259-2 are mappings, not implicit conformance.
When catalogues conflict (uniqueness, usability 2013 versus 2023, precision versus uncertainty, credibility versus coverage), persist the conflict code and the local canonical meaning.
Consumers MUST accept both a single-score projection and a multi-dimension set; dropping dimensions is a view, not a canonical merge.
Older ISO 19157:2013 usability scores MAY be imported as extensions, never as ISO 19157-1:2023 core elements.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier of the quality assertion, certificate or catalogue entry.
Governed global identifier or IRI in the Dimension or standard namespace.
UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension when no master or governed IRI exists.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All event, validity, generation, invalidation and ingestion times use RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z; record evaluation event time and observation/ingestion time separately; a timestamp is never used as an identifier.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artefacts use {namespace}/{artefact-type}/{assertion-or-catalogue-id}/{version} with lower-kebab-case types such as measurement-observation, uncertainty-budget, certificate-document, evidence-pack; do not encode dates as the identifying path segment.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Serial artefacts that are evidence, certificates or procedures carry an integrity hash of their bytes; QualityMetadata bundles record member hashes so adding a statement yields a new bundle identity.

policies: Quality measurements are observations: append and invalidate, do not mutate historical values.
Do not claim standard conformance without a conformance statement that cites measurements or an explicit not-evaluated status.
Predictive or rater confidence SHALL NOT be labelled as GUM expanded uncertainty or statistical confidence interval without a documented calibration and distributional justification.
Independent review is required before a Dimension treats a quality result as authoritative for high-impact decisions, consistent with NIST Measure guidance.
Access to quality records defaults to need-to-know; publication of scores that reveal security or personal data requires a documented exception.

read: Quality consumers with scope grants may read measurements, summaries and public certificates.
Auditors and independent reviewers may read evidence packs and provenance bundles.
Public read of detailed defect-level measurements is off by default.
create: Authorised assessors and software agents may create measurements, annotations and evidence packs.
Only listed certifying bodies may create certificate annotations.
Dimension stewards may create catalogue entries.
update: Metadata corrections that do not change the observed value may add errata linked by derivation.
Lifecycle updates are invalidation, supersession, revocation or access-policy changes.
In-place edit of dqv:value is forbidden.
delete: Hard delete is allowed only after retention expiry and no legal hold, and SHOULD leave a tombstone of assertion_id, invalidation time and deletion event.
Superseded statements are invalidated, not deleted, while still inside retention.

roles.name: Quality steward
responsibilities: Own the local dimension and metric catalogue, namespace and crosswalks.
Approve extensions and record mapping conflicts.

roles.name: Quality assessor
responsibilities: Run evaluation procedures and generate measurements.
Attach evidence and declare construct codes for confidence fields.

roles.name: Independent reviewer
responsibilities: Review methods, test-set representativity and evidence sufficiency.
Mitigate assessor bias for authoritative results.

roles.name: Certifying body
responsibilities: Issue, suspend and revoke quality certificates within a named scheme.
Ensure certificate documents have integrity hashes and stated coverage.

roles.name: Quality consumer
responsibilities: Interpret scores against stated purpose, method and uncertainty.
Must not treat a single undocumented composite as complete quality.

roles.name: Host record owner
responsibilities: Supply correct host identifiers and notify quality stewards of host revisions that trigger refresh.
Does not unilaterally overwrite independent assessments.

access.default_rule: Need-to-know read for quality measurements and evidence; catalogue definitions may be broader; public scores require an explicit publication grant and sensitivity review.
exceptions: Public certificate summaries may be released without evidence packs.
Personal comments in user feedback may be redacted or restricted even when the score is public.
Security-relevant availability or vulnerability-related quality findings follow the security sibling model's disclosure timeline.
Legal hold blocks deletion but does not by itself expand read access.
audit_requirements: Record create, invalidate, revoke, access-grant change and evidence-pack download events with RFC 3339 time, actor and assertion_id.
Retain audit logs at least as long as the quality evidence they refer to.

read_order: AGENTS.md in the quality mixin package root
Specification URL (this model and local profile)
Dimension catalogue of dimensions and metrics
Storage type URL and Interface URL
Processes URL for evaluate, certify, invalidate and retain
Host identity and PROV reference models

coverage.claim: Defensible mixin coverage of quality dimensions, metric methods, scores, fitness context, policy/conformance, evidence and confidence/uncertainty as distinct constructs, grounded in W3C DQV, ISO/IEC 25012, ISO 19157-1, ISO 8000-1, JCGM GUM, NIST AI RMF and ISO/IEC 5259-2, without claiming a universal quality ontology or full-text access to every paid ISO clause.

checklist.notes: Assertion, dimension, metric, policy, certificate, quality-unit and evidence identifiers with master/IRI/UUID priority; dates excluded as identifiers.
Generation, validity window, invalidation, supersession, refresh triggers, certificate revocation and catalogue versioning.
Host binding, inverse quality lists, derivation among measurements, conflicting annotations, policy targets and certificate coverage.
Separate evaluation event time and ingestion time; host temporal extent; currentness windows; statement validity interval; RFC 3339.
PROV generation, attribution, delegation, used entities and QualityMetadata bundles for assessments, distinct from host lineage.
Attributed agents, stewards, certifying bodies, annotator roles and acted-on-behalf-of.
Conformance outcomes, independent review, representativity of test sets, incomplete uncertainty flags and explicit non-conformance.
Need-to-know default, scoped grants, sensitivity classification; ISO/IEC 25012 accessibility/confidentiality treated as aligned dimensions only.
Retention period, legal hold, tombstone delete, evidence-pack retention and audit-log retention.
Crosswalks to DQV, ISO/IEC 25012, ISO 19157-1, GUM, ISO/IEC 5259-2 and PROV with conflict register and no silent conformance.
GUM Type A/B, expanded uncertainty, coverage probability, metaquality confidence and predictive scores as separate constructs.
Context of use, purpose identifiers, limitations of use and policy-stated minima rather than ISO 19157-implied thresholds.
Census versus sample, empty-unit exceptions, expected-use test sets and homogeneity/disaggregation.
ISO 19157-1 metaquality elements: confidence in the evaluation, representativity and homogeneity.

known_omissions: Full clause-level text of ISO/IEC 25012, ISO 19157-1, ISO 8000 parts beyond Part 1 overview, ISO/IEC 25024 measure tables and ISO/IEC 5259-2 additional ML characteristic names was not available as free complete primary HTML; those names must be copied from licensed text before claiming a closed catalogue.
JCGM GUM-1:2023 Bayesian/coverage-interval restatement is only partially cited via secondary catalogue notices; this model remains aligned to JCGM 100:2008/2010 as fetched.
UNECE NQAF, SDMX quality reporting, DDI quality statements, HL7 FHIR/clinical quality measures and FAIR metrics are not modelled; they are likely specialised siblings.
ISO 5725 accuracy of measurement methods, JCGM 200 VIM vocabulary and ISO/IEC 17025 calibration certificates are not fully incorporated.
Wang and Strong 1996 academic dimension set and DAMA-DMBOK uniqueness/validity are used only as conflict notes, not as primary catalogues.
Qualitative uncertainty for nominal classifications lacks a single primary standard comparable to GUM.
Region-specific legal accuracy duties (for example GDPR accuracy principle) are not encoded as legislation objects.
conflicts: DQV refuses a universal definition of quality; ISO/IEC 25012 enumerates fifteen characteristics as a data-quality model. Both are alignments.
ISO 19157:2013 included a usability element; ISO 19157-1:2023 does not keep usability as a core element.
Uniqueness is common in DAMA-style lists but is not an ISO/IEC 25012 characteristic.
ISO 8000 treats relevant characteristics as purpose-dependent; some operational scorecards treat accuracy as intrinsic.
GUM coverage probability or level of confidence is not the same construct as ISO/IEC 25012 credibility, ISO 19157 metaquality confidence, or ML/rater confidence scores.
Precision in ISO/IEC 25012 and DQV (resolution) is not GUM precision/repeatability and not expanded uncertainty.
ISO/IEC 25012 confidentiality, accessibility and availability overlap sibling access/privacy/availability models.
regional_assumptions: ISO, W3C, BIPM/JCGM and NIST sources are treated as globally citable technical authorities; they are not a substitute for jurisdictional quality-of-data law.
GUM k approximately 2 for about 95 percent coverage assumes a near-normal case; other distributions need explicit justification.
Positional accuracy, topological consistency and gridded accuracy apply when the host is geographic or otherwise spatially referenced.
NIST AI RMF is a voluntary US public-authority framework; ISO/IEC 5259 is the international AI data-quality measures standard.
adversarial_checks: Rejected treating a model softmax or star rating as GUM expanded uncertainty without calibration evidence.
Rejected using a report date as the quality assertion identifier.
